signals.title: A Study on the Mechanism and Ways to Improve New-Quality Productivity of Enterprises Driven by AI and the Digital Economy
signals.abstract: With the deep development of the digital economy and the accelerated iteration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, the formation and development of enterprise new quality productive forces have attracted increasing attention from academia and practice. Based on enterprises as the micro-subject, this paper constructs a theoretical analysis framework for the "dual-wheel drive of AI and the digital economy" and explores the formation mechanism and the path to enhancing the synergistic empowerment of enterprise these forces. The research finds that AI and the digital economy are not simply parallel drivers, but form a synergistic empowerment effect through a triple interactive mechanism of "technology-factor-organization." AI technology reshapes the technological boundary of the production function, while the digital economy reconstructs the allocation logic of production factors.

signals.title: Putting place first: towards a new vision for UK industrial strategy
signals.abstract: This paper challenges the longstanding dominance of agglomeration theory in shaping the UK’s approach to industrial and regional strategy. While agglomeration thinking, rooted in urban economics, has played an influential role in government policy for two decades, persistent spatial inequalities, institutional fragmentation and the underperformance of the UK’s largest cities raise serious questions about its suitability as a universal framework for national industrial policy. The paper argues that the UK economy is better understood as comprising three distinct types of firm–place relationships: agglomeration economies, industrial complex economies and social network economies. signals.title: Envisioning Mortgage Futures
signals.abstract: This paper explores how open banking and algorithmic profiling are reshaping mortgage lending in the UK. Drawing on interviews with lenders, brokers, technology developers and borrowers, it examines how transaction data, behavioural analytics and predictive modelling are being used to assess credit risk. While these technologies promise efficiency and inclusion, they often deepen inequality by embedding opaque and morally charged judgements into lending decisions. signals.abstract: ABSTRACT Resource efficiency has become a priority for the European agri‐food sector, yet adoption remains uneven across countries and firms. This study examines how European agri‐food small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) adopt resource efficiency practices. signals.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
signals.abstract: This paper investigates how AI practitioners in India perceive and experience Responsible AI (RAI) through mixed-method qualitative research with participants from industry and academia. We argue that RAI practice in India operates as a doubly hegemonic system in which global Western frameworks that privilege technical and procedural conceptions of responsibility converge with local caste-gender hierarchies to determine what counts as legitimate ethical knowledge. signals.title: Watermelon vine as dual-functional additive in ecological porous concrete
signals.abstract: Ecological porous concrete (EPC) is constrained by a persistent trade-off: the dense cementitious matrix required for strength reduces porosity and generates a highly alkaline pore environment (pH > 11) inimical to plant growth. To address this, the present study investigates watermelon vine (WV), an abundant agricultural waste, as a dual-functional additive that simultaneously provides physical reinforcement and chemical alkalinity regulation. signals.title: Antimicrobial and antioxidant activity of Zataria multiflora essential oil and its delivery systems in food
signals.abstract: Zataria multiflora , known as Avishane Shirazi (Shirazi thyme) or Persian thyme, is one of the most popular aromatic and medicinal plants in Iran. Zataria multiflora essential oil (ZEO) has been reported to have various biological activities. The studies showed that ZEO had significant antioxidant and antimicrobial activities, and its application in various foods yielded promising results in maintaining the chemical and microbiological quality of foods. This review focused on the chemical composition, antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal activities of ZEO. Furthermore, this review summarized the food preservation applications of ZEO (direct addition or use in packaging materials such as coating and film), and its delivery systems (encapsulation methods) in food. ZEO can be considered as one of the most promising alternatives for food preservation.

signals.title: Comparative assessment of low-carbon energy pathways for agricultural heat and power production
signals.abstract: Agriculture has an important role in the transition to a low-carbon economy, but the sector still relies heavily on fossil fuels for heat and electricity production. This study compares alternative pathways for supplying heat, electricity, and combined heat and power in agricultural applications. signals.title: How do we plan from here? Innovative planning practices in rural areas facing demographic realities
signals.abstract: This paper explores how a realistic and innovative planning approach can address demographic challenges in rural areas. It tests the Rural Planning and Innovation Lab, a strategic planning model that has been implemented in Switzerland, Sweden and Norway. The test indicates that the model serves as a vehicle for the development of innovative strategies, thus supporting place-baced strategies that can make paradigm shifts possible. The study underscores the need to decouple development from population growth, which enables planning in shrinking regions through collaboration between planning authorities and civil society. We contribute to the discussion and further development of innovative planning models.

signals.title: Analyzing the cultural landscape of Chinese art districts through online social media: a text mining and theoretical interpretation using user-generated content
signals.abstract: Abstract The study examines three Chinese art districts—Beijing 798, Hangzhou Xiangshan, and Jingdezhen Taoxichuan—using 28,661 social media posts. Integrating LDA modeling, irony-aware sentiment analysis, and semantic networks, it uncovers tensions among commercialization, cultural authenticity, and urban identity. Findings reveal 31.2% negative sentiment toward Beijing 798’s over-commercialization, 63.8% positivity for Jingdezhen’s heritage revitalization, and 40% neutrality toward Hangzhou’s emerging spaces. Advancing Lefebvre’s spatial triad, a dynamic equilibrium framework is proposed to balance heritage and development. Methodologically, blending digital humanities tools with cultural theory offers insights into urban renewal and participatory placemaking in the digital era.

signals.title: A Mobile Edge Computing and Blockchain Framework for Secure Cross-Island Critical Mineral Traceability
signals.venue: International Journal of Interactive Mobile Technologies (iJIM)
signals.abstract: Cloud-based traceability systems depend on continuous connectivity, limiting their reliability in geographically dispersed mineral supply chains where prolonged network outages may occur. This study proposes an offline-first architecture integrating Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) with a permissioned blockchain for secure cross-island critical-mineral traceability. Traceability events generated at mines, transport routes, ports, vessels, warehouses, and processing facilities are locally validated, digitally signed, encrypted, and queued at MEC gateways during connectivity loss before synchronization with the blockchain. signals.title: Circular Economy and E‐Waste Management: A Comprehensive Bibliometric Analysis and Systematic Literature Review (2005–2026)

signals.title: Fictions, Frictions & Evictions: Housing Data Stories
signals.venue: Maynooth University ePrints and eTheses Archive (Maynooth University)
signals.abstract: A collection of 208 drabbles – stories of exactly 100 words – that shine a spotlight on the data politics of housing, property and planning data. Written over a four year period, the drabbles are inspired by conversations and observations while undertaking empirical research on the Data Stories project. Collectively, they reveal the ways in which the housing, property and planning evidence base in Ireland is less than ideal and point to what needs to be done to address the shortcomings.

signals.title: From Public to Private Governance, and Back—Eco‐Modulation as De‐Privatization in Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)
signals.abstract: ABSTRACT The European Union is advancing circular economy policies, aimed at reducing the environmental impacts of products across their life‐cycles. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) exemplifies this strategy. It privatizes the end‐of‐life management of products to their producers, seeking thereby to incentivize the producer to design environmentally more sustainable products. However, EPR has failed to deliver significant improvements in product design. This article examines the EU's attempts to strengthen eco‐design in EPR through ‘eco‐modulation’. Applying the theory of competence‐and‐control, the article argues that the introduction of eco‐modulation will destabilize the public‐private balance in EPR, shifting EPR back from private towards public governance.
